ai.description: This skink reaches 5 cm snout-vent length. It is bronze-brown with a dark lateral stripe and pale belly. It features a long, slender body and small, smooth scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: To distinguish *Subdoluseps bowringii*, look for the absence of a distinct dark dorsolateral stripe, which is typically present in similar Indian skinks like *Eutropis* species.
ai.habitat: *Subdoluseps bowringii* inhabits moist, low-altitude environments, typically found in leaf litter within tropical forests, gardens, and urban areas across the Indian subcontinent.
ai.behavior: The Christmas Island Grass-Skink is primarily diurnal, actively foraging for small insects and invertebrates among leaf litter and low-lying vegetation during the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Subdoluseps bowringii* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 2–4 eggs. Breeding occurs throughout the year, peaking during the monsoon season in India.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Subdoluseps bowringii* is found across parts of Northeast India and the Andaman Islands, typically inhabiting low-to-mid elevation forests and disturbed habitats.
